facts.text: Wayland began as Crooked Creek, settled in the late 1830s, and became a voting precinct on October 5, 1840.
In 1880, Wayland adopted its current name during railroad negotiations, replacing Marshall to avoid mail confusion with another Iowa town.
A log‑cabin Methodist Episcopal church was erected in 1844, showcasing the early influence of Methodist settlers in Wayland.
Mennonite families of German heritage began arriving in the late 1850s, with a surge in the late 1890s, shaping Wayland’s cultural fabric.
Wayland sits on gently rolling plains, historically bounded by the Skunk River to the east and Crooked Creek to the south.
Wayland’s high school relocated there in 1989, bringing a new generation of students to the community.
